channel.description: Verified case files located in Global.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Fake Web3 accelerator uses npm packages to spread malware and hijack AI agent traffic
item.description: Elastic Security Labs (REF8801) found a fake Web3 'Apex Accelerator' luring crypto founders with free AI credits, coding tools and audits via two npm packages, @apexacc/cli (a repackaged open-source coding agent) and @apexacc/audit (an MCP audit tool). The packages deliver information stealers and backdoors on Windows and macOS and write an MCP entry that redirects AI agent requests to attacker-controlled services. Elastic did not observe malicious substitution of AI responses and no victim count has been published. Target: Developers installing npm packages; AI agent traffic. Global. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Yoba malware spread via fake ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps on GitHub
item.description: Check Point Research reports a two-month campaign (Yoba) using fake GitHub projects posing as AI desktop apps (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus), placing malware beside legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables for DLL sideloading; the observed final payload was an XMRig cryptominer, though the loader can deliver any payload. Target: Users seeking ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps. Global. Verification: reported.
